chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Shaybani, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Imran al-Nakha'i narrated to us, from his paternal uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid, from Isma'il ibn Muslim, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali (peace be upon them).

He said: Jibra'il descended upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family) and said: 'O Muhammad, order your companions to 'ajj and thajj.' 'Ajj is raising the voices with talbiyah, and thajj is slaughtering the sacrificial animals.'

key_terms.الثَّجُّ: Slaughtering or cutting (specifically of sacrificial animals)
key_terms.الْتَّلْبِيَةِ: The declaration of 'Here I am, O Allah' (talbiyah)
key_terms.الْعَجُّ: Raising the voice in supplication or declaration (specifically talbiyah)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'ajj and thajj in the context of Hajj rituals?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, this hadith provides a concise exegetical definition of the ritual terms 'ajj and thajj as they appear in the Quranic verses on Hajj. It clarifies that 'ajj denotes the vocal proclamation of the talbiyah, while thajj specifically refers to the slaughter of the sacrificial animal, thereby linking linguistic precision to the physical acts of worship. This interpretation is significant in Shia scholarship for understanding the specific ritualistic components of the Hajj pilgrimage as commanded by the Angel Jibra'il.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Muhammed bin Ahmad al-Shaybani, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Abi Abdillah al-Kufi, that he said: We were told by Musa bin Imran al-Nakha’I, from his paternal uncle, Hussain bin Yazid, from Isma’eel ibn Muslim, from Ja’far bin Muhammed, from his father, from his grandfather, from Ali, peace be upon them, that he said:

Jibra’eel descended unto the Prophet, Allah’s blessings be upon him and his Family, and said: O Muhammed, order you companions to ‘ajj and thajj. ‘Ajj is to raise the voices during declaring gratification (to Allah), and thajj is to slaughter the cattle.
